findings.title: Global group manage check grants manage permission for view-only permissions
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller has either VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource. Global manage should require MANAGE only. This method is used by GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() via requireManage(), so a principal with only view permission on all groups can create top-level groups. The check should use only AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. hasPermission() expects the group ID, which is stored as the authorization resource name for instance resources, not the internal authorization resource ID. As a result, group-specific VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions are not found, and the method can return internal resource IDs (including the ID of the all-groups type resource) instead of realm group IDs. User search and user count filtering that relies on these IDs will then return wrong results or no results. It should use the resource name for instance resources and skip the Groups type resource.

findings.title: Individual authorization resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() creates instance resources for Clients, Groups, and Users but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() relies on resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) to locate group instance resources. Without the type being set, those instance resources will not be returned by findByType(), so group-scoped member permissions cannot be collected. The resource type should be set when creating the resource.

findings.title: All-groups permissions are ignored whenever a group-specific resource exists
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to the all-groups type resource only when no resource exists for the requested group ID. If a group-specific resource exists, permissions attached to the all-groups resource are not evaluated at all. This means an all-groups MANAGE or VIEW_MEMBERS grant can be shadowed by the mere existence of a group-specific resource, even if that resource does not grant the requested scope, leading to unexpected forbidden operations. Evaluation should consider both the instance resource and the type resource, or fall back when the instance resource does not grant the requested scopes.

findings.title: Existing realms are not initialized with the new Groups scopes and resources
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns immediately if realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() already exists. Realms that were initialized before this change will not get the new Groups resource type or the manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members scopes. Subsequent group permission evaluation or resource creation can fail because the Groups type resource or required scopes are missing. An idempotent initialization or migration is needed to add missing schema objects to existing realms.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException in getScope for missing or unknown resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope() dereferences SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType) without checking whether resourceType is null or whether the map lookup returns null. If this method is called with a missing or unsupported resource type, it will throw a NullPointerException and likely produce an HTTP 500 instead of a validation error. The resource type should be validated before accessing its scopes.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when Groups type resource is missing
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource). getResourceTypeResource() can return null if the Groups type resource has not been initialized, which would cause a NullPointerException. A null check should return false or throw a meaningful exception.

findings.title: Missing return when brute force protection is disabled
findings.body: BruteForceUsersResource.getBruteForceStatus() sets default brute force status when realm.isBruteForceProtected() is false but does not return. The method then continues to look up login failures and may overwrite the default status with stale failure data even though brute force protection is disabled. It should return after setting the default status when brute force protection is off.

findings.title: Group resource names are not resolved for display
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName() only resolves Users resources to a human-readable username. For Groups resources it falls back to resource.getDisplayName(), but group instance resources are created with the group ID as the name and no display name. As a result, group resources can be shown as raw group IDs in admin-facing responses. Group resources should be resolved to their group name, or a display name should be set when creating the resource.
